title: VS Code and Git
summary: `code --wait` as Git's editor, VS Code as diff and merge tool, and the merge editor for conflicts.

steps.title: Why --wait matters
body: When Git needs a message (a plain `git commit`, `git rebase -i`, `git merge` without `-m`), it starts `core.editor` on a file and **waits for that program to exit**, then reads the file.

`code file` hands the file to the VS Code window and exits at once. Git sees an exit, reads a still-empty file and stops: **Aborting commit due to empty commit message.** `--wait` (`-w`) makes `code` stay until you close that tab.
The same flag makes VS Code usable for `git difftool` and `git mergetool`, and for `crontab -e` or `kubectl edit` through `EDITOR="code --wait"`.

steps.prompt: After `git config --global core.editor code`, every `git commit` (without `-m`) ends at once with `Aborting commit due to empty commit message.` Why?
options: `code` returns as soon as the file is open, so Git reads the message before you type it
VS Code cannot edit files in `.git/`
Git needs `core.editor` to be a full path
The commit has no staged changes
steps.explain: Git waits for the editor process to exit. Without `--wait`, the process exits immediately. `git config --global core.editor "code --wait"` fixes it.

steps.title: Diff, merge and the merge editor
body: The `code` command line does more than open files:
| `code --merge LOCAL REMOTE BASE RESULT` | three-way merge editor |
Make it Git's diff and merge tool (these are the commands from the VS Code docs):

Inside VS Code, a conflicted file shows **Accept Current / Accept Incoming / Accept Both** above each conflict, and a **Resolve in Merge Editor** button that opens the three-way view: incoming and current on top, the result below.

steps.prompt: Make VS Code the editor Git waits for, then open the result of a merge conflict in its merge editor.
Does Git wait for you to finish in VS Code?
buckets: Git does not wait (or opens no editor)

steps.prompt: `core.editor` is `code --wait` (set globally), and you also exported `GIT_EDITOR=nano` in this shell. What does `git var GIT_EDITOR` print?
steps.explain: The `GIT_EDITOR` environment variable beats every config setting. That is handy for one command (`GIT_EDITOR=true git rebase --continue` accepts the prepared message) and confusing when it is left in your shell profile.

steps.title: Every commit aborts
prompt: In `~/shop` a README fix is staged, but `git commit` keeps failing. Run it and read the message.
1. Find which `core.editor` Git uses (`git var GIT_EDITOR`, `git config --show-origin --get-all core.editor`) and fix it globally so Git waits for VS Code.
2. Make VS Code Git's diff tool and merge tool (`diff.tool` / `merge.tool` `vscode`, with the `difftool.vscode.cmd` and `mergetool.vscode.cmd` commands from the lesson).
3. Run `git commit` again: it should go through.

VS Code is not installed in this container. A small stand-in for its `code` launcher is: like the real one it returns at once without `--wait`, and with `--wait` it acts as if you typed the message `Fix README typo` and closed the tab.

checks.name: VS Code is the diff tool
checks.cmd: git config --global diff.tool && git config --global difftool.vscode.cmd
checks.fail: Set `diff.tool` to `vscode` and `difftool.vscode.cmd` to `code --wait --diff $LOCAL $REMOTE` (single quotes, so the shell does not expand `$LOCAL`).

checks.name: VS Code is the merge tool
checks.cmd: git config --global merge.tool && git config --global mergetool.vscode.cmd

hints: `git commit` prints `Aborting commit due to empty commit message.` `git var GIT_EDITOR` says `code`: no `--wait`.
`git config --global diff.tool vscode`, `git config --global difftool.vscode.cmd 'code --wait --diff $LOCAL $REMOTE'`, and the same pair for `merge.tool` / `mergetool.vscode.cmd`.
steps.explain: `git var GIT_EDITOR` answers "what will Git run?" in one line, whatever mix of `GIT_EDITOR`, `core.editor`, `VISUAL` and `EDITOR` is set. With the tools configured, `git difftool main` and `git mergetool` during a conflict open VS Code and wait for you.
